title: The good shepherd (John 10:1–18)
hookLine: he knows his sheep by name and they know his voice

lines: YOUR NAME IN A CROWDED AIRPORT.
cards: In a crowded airport, a hundred voices blur into noise. Then someone far off says your name, and your head turns before you've decided anything.

Travelers in the Middle East have described something like it with sheep: several flocks sheltering together overnight, all mixed up, and in the morning each shepherd simply calls, and his own sheep sort themselves out and follow him.
The man born blind has just been thrown out of the synagogue. Right after, Jesus starts talking about sheep, voices and names.

teach.h: THE FOLD, THE GATE, THE THIEF.
teach.b: Jesus sets the scene: a sheepfold, a wall, a gate, a keeper at the gate. A thief climbs over the wall.
The shepherd comes in by the door, and the Douay-Rheims says: "the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out." Name first, then leading.
He doesn't drive them from behind with a stick; he walks ahead, and they follow a voice they know. Then another great I am: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep."

teach.h: THE HIRED HAND RUNS; HE STAYS.
teach.b: A hired hand sees the wolf coming and runs, because the sheep aren't his.

teach.h: THE SHEPHERD ON THE CATACOMB WALL.
teach.b: The good shepherd stays, and more than stays. John's word for good, kalos, also carries the sense of beautiful, noble, the real thing.

Then a line about outsiders: other sheep I have, that are not of this fold; them also I must bring. Whatever else that means, the flock is bigger than the people standing there. And look where John sets this speech.
A man has just been pushed out of his community for telling the truth, and Jesus went looking for him. The shepherd keeps the one who was thrown out.
Some of the oldest Christian paintings, on the walls of the Roman catacombs, show a young shepherd with a lamb across his shoulders.
And the fourth Sunday of Easter is called Good Shepherd Sunday, when the Church prays for vocations, for people called to shepherd others.

how: On the fourth Sunday of Easter, Good Shepherd Sunday, Catholics hear a reading from John 10 at Mass, and the Church prays that day for vocations to the priesthood and religious life.

games.q: you're a hired hand watching someone else's sheep, and a wolf comes over the hill. what does Jesus say a hired hand does?
games.why: the hired hand runs, because the sheep aren't his. the good shepherd is the one who stays and gives his life.

practice: Let the sounds around you come in, traffic, a fan, a bird, your own breath, without chasing any of them. Then, under all the noise, imagine your own first name said once, quietly, by someone who means you well, and let it land.
If you pray, hold the line, he calleth his own sheep by name; if not, rest in the feeling of being known by name.

wordCard.voice: Kalos. The Greek word for good that also means noble, beautiful: what Jesus calls the shepherd who calls his own by name and lays down his life for them. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the good shepherd (John 10:11). kalos also means noble, beautiful.
